before_body:
Planning matching family Christmas photo outfits for 2026 starts with the picture you want to keep. A sofa cuddle, a Christmas morning tree photo and an outdoor holiday card portrait each suggest a different outfit. Choose your setting first, then build everyone's clothing around it.

For a home session, leave room for movement and a few pauses. For a professional mini session, choose one complete look and arrive dressed. Whether you want everyone in the same pattern or simply sharing colors, plan the whole outfit, including whatever will show below the knees.

Pick a look: pajamas or sweaters

Pajamas suit cozy at-home pictures, Christmas morning and sitting beside the tree. For a simple starting point, Classic Red Plaid pajamas pair solid red tops with red tartan pants. If you want a message across the tops, We Are Family Red pajamas combine black and white lettering with red plaid pants.

Choose Evergreen Fair Isle pajamas for green and white bands of trees, reindeer and snowflakes across both pieces. Let It Snow pajamas offer another direction: red tops with navy and white lettering, plus red, white and navy plaid pants. Keep the surrounding blankets and cushions plain when choosing either patterned look.

For a family including a baby, consider Snowflake Reindeer hooded onesies, which have Baby sizes alongside Mother, Father and Child sizes. The hoods have reindeer ears and antlers; try a seated group picture with everyone close together.

Sweaters work for outdoor portraits and daytime card photos with trousers or jeans. Start with your preferred main color: Jingle Bells Santa sweaters show a waving Santa on deep green, while Santa Hat Reindeer sweaters put a cream reindeer face and white snowflakes on red.

For navy, consider the cream band of reindeer faces on Nordic Heart Reindeer sweaters or the tan reindeer across the white chest of Reindeer Row sweaters. For a tree-themed picture, Santa Tree Topper sweaters show Santa placing a star on a Christmas tree. For an outdoor mini session, plan suitable layers and ask your photographer where coats can stay between pictures.

Before packing a second look for a mini session, confirm whether an outfit change fits the appointment. Keep shoes, socks and any agreed prop together so everyone can get dressed without searching for missing pieces.

Coordinating colors and patterns

Choose red, green or navy as your main color, then repeat one supporting color across the group. A red and navy palette can start with the plaid pants in Plaid Tree Trio pajamas. For green and white, use We Are Family Evergreen pajamas, with white tops, dark green sleeves and green and red plaid pants.

For a mix of sweater designs, repeat a color already in the pattern. The red chest and navy bands of Nordic Reindeer sweaters suggest navy bottoms across the family. Lay everyone's clothes side by side before deciding; include any hats or layers you expect to keep on.

Pair patterned pants with solid tops when assembling a coordinated look from your own clothes. With patterned sweaters, try plain dark jeans, navy trousers or cream bottoms. Choose one general direction for the group so the lower half of the picture feels connected.

For indoor pajama pictures, choose plain socks in a shared color. For outdoor sweater photos, coordinate practical shoes or boots and check which socks show when everyone sits. Try the whole outfit seated as well as standing.

Sizing and timing

Every piece is sold separately per person. Select each family member's role and size individually: pajamas come in Mother, Father and Child sizes, with Baby sizes also offered in the hooded onesie style above. Sweaters come in unisex Adult and Child sizes. Open “Size guide & fit” on each product page and compare each person's measurements with that specific guide.

If siblings wear different designs, check both size guides before choosing. During the try-on, have everyone sit, reach forward and bend their knees. Practice holding a child or sitting together in the position you want photographed.

Standard shipping is included. Each product page shows estimated delivery, currently about 12–16 days after ordering. For US orders, product pages currently show estimated arrival before Christmas when ordering by December 8. Check the product page for the current estimate before placing your order.

Photo sessions usually happen earlier than Christmas, so work backward from your session date. Order early enough to leave extra time beyond the estimated delivery window for a family try-on. For holiday cards, allow time after the session to choose pictures and arrange printing. Read the 30-day returns policy as part of your planning.

Posing and setup ideas

  • Start with one clear background. Choose the tree, a plain wall or a sofa. Move everyday clutter out of the frame and take a test picture before gathering everyone.
  • Try a window-facing setup. At home, position the family facing a window and check the test image for shadows. Adjust your position before asking children to settle.
  • Build a seated group. Sit adults first, then bring children close alongside or on laps. Keep faces visible and check that folded arms do not cover every sweater design.
  • Give everyone something to do. Read a book together, look toward the tree or ask siblings to share a joke. Take a few pictures between the more formal poses.
  • Plan the card frame. Ask for a horizontal and a vertical picture, with space around the family for cropping. For a professional mini session, share your priority groupings beforehand.

A simple checklist

  • Confirm the photo date, setting and card layout.
  • Choose pajamas or sweaters and a shared palette.
  • Select each person's outfit separately.
  • Check every product's size guide.
  • Check estimated delivery against the session date.
  • Try on bottoms, shoes, socks and layers together.
  • Prepare your background and priority poses.

Start with matching family Christmas outfits to choose your shared look. For more help with either direction, read our Christmas pajama guide and our Christmas sweater guide. Then set out everyone's outfit together, leaving the photo session itself for getting close and spending a little time as a family.
